# Grow light buying notes

## What I wanted

Something to sit over the seed trays from February to April, and to help the houseplants through December. The old T5 tubes from school do the seedlings well enough (see [[Seed starting under lights]]) but cover only half a shelf and one tube is flickering. Budget £70, less if possible.

## The shortlist

### Lumora GL-640

Full-spectrum LED panel, 65 W actual draw, 60 x 30 cm. Claimed PPFD 310 at 30 cm. Daisy-chain socket. £64.99 at Garden Lighting Direct. White light, not the purple glow, which matters because it's in the spare room and I have to walk past.

### Brightfield BX-22 bars

Two 45 cm bars, 22 W each, clip-on. £39 for the pair. Light spread is narrow, the reviews said good for one tray but not two.

### The market one

Purple "UFO" from the Saturday market in Newton Abbot, £25, no brand, no wattage on the box, the man said "about a hundred watts" while looking at his phone. No.

## The deciding numbers

| | Watts | Coverage | Price | £ per watt |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lumora GL-640 | 65 | 2 trays | £64.99 | 1.00 |
| Brightfield BX-22 x2 | 44 | 1 tray | £39.00 | 0.89 |

Alfie checked the GL-640 with a phone light meter app: about 290 at tray height, near enough to the claim.

## Bought

Lumora GL-640, order GLD-88213, 9 January 2025, delivered 13 January. Hung on two adjustable ratchet hangers (£7.50 extra). Put it all in the gardening column of the [[Budget spreadsheet]].

## Afterthoughts

The panel gets warm, 38°C on the back after two hours, so it must hang at least 25 cm above seedlings. Used it on the fig for a few weeks too, see [[Fiddle leaf fig leaf drop]]. Wish I'd bought the timer with it.
